RFCLI (/workplace/.../PrimaryInstallation/src/ReactiveFiberCLI): the first commit whose context.render.schema.json defines result.speculative is 8bd35ecd4651 ('[RF-WM-R3-e] --scenario served on rf context render for cli', 2026-10-24, __version__.py VERSION 0.1.844); its $defs/result states the nine scenarioResultKeys 'present exactly on a `rf context render --scenario PATH` render ... and absent on a legacy or --view render', the same nine at origin/main c83fbd59ec1c (VERSION 0.1.845) and in the installed rf 0.1.845 schema (sha256 in measured). The marker keys and labels are application/scenario_view.py WHATIF_RESULT_KEY 'speculative', NOTICE_BLOCK_KEY 'rf.whatif_notice' and WhatIfNotice.text's opening 'WHAT-IF VIEW of scenario ', and domain/scenario.py SCENARIO_ID_MARKER_KEY 'rf.scenario_id' and EPISTEMIC_STATUS_MARKER_KEY 'rf.epistemic_status' (block and notice metadata); rendered_speculative_view is the design name of 02-architecture.md:9@82bd879eee52, spelled by no release; scenario_id and scenario are the scenario identity keys, which no 0.1.784 or 0.1.845 schema property spells outside a scenario member. The pin at the cut's base dc72a6d: RFCLI 403389a94 ('chore: bump version to 0.1.784') holds 28 result properties, none of the nine, and no marker or label string; recorded as provenance only (no case asserts it), so the queued re-pin wb-jwc.4 (0.1.845) moves nothing in this census. scenarioSample and scenarioBlock are CAPTURED: the nine members and the one block of a real `rf --workspace W context render --scenario scenario.json --audience cli --no-input --json` at the installed rf 0.1.845 (rc 0, ok true), in a disposable workspace W=/tmp/ws02-s110-grmo1-rfws provisioned by the rf-preview recipe of docs/workbench/receipts/wb-c7ku.md (rf init --backend jsonl --no-input; rf component create --kind declarative demo.banner; rf component add of its manifest; rf component activate demo.banner; rf graph validate; all rc 0), over one committed render of that workspace, with a reactive-fiber.scenario/v1 document whose one action is {source_id task, type set_source, value }; the nine members carry no workspace path, id or timestamp. The same capture holds its notice in result.notice only (result.blocks is the one component block) and output.text opens with the notice line. Through the helper's diffAgainstRoster against this SCG-R11 roster the capture gives the 12 speculative entries B4 pins (the nine members, the two block markers, the output.text label), while a real --no-commit render of Pi's own legacy argv in the same workspace gives 0 speculative entries (its only failures are the pre-existing 0.1.784 to 0.1.845 drift keys judge_context, judge_context_layers and replay_of_operation_id). The members also pass the seat's structural check against the installed schema (required, additionalProperties false, enum, const, digest pattern; not a schema engine). wb-dkru (seat ws-01, g10-work-s119, 2026-10-27; R694 follow-up from the wb-grmo.1 landing 545 gate cmd_c44799b3bdfd, its F3 and F4), MEASURED by the cutting seat and not re-read by the census: marked 18.0.11 (the devDependency, marked.parseInline) renders spec*ul*ative, spec**ul**ative, spec***ul***ative, spec~ul~ative, spec~~ul~~ative and spec`ul`ative as em, strong, del or code inside one word, and spec​*ul*ative with its emphasis; it shows spec_ul_ative, spec__ul__ative, spec\*ul\*ative and spec*ul*ative with their marks, escapes spec­ulative (no ';') to show it as written, and renders spec[ul](...)ative as a link inside the word. NAMED_REFERENCE_LIST is read off Python 3.12.15 html.entities.html5 (2231 entries, 2125 names written with ';'): the 309 names whose value, its format characters removed and NFKC applied, is empty or holds an ASCII letter, digit or '_', JS white space, or one of . ! ? \ * ` ~ - and the ten dash look-alikes, then the 10 names whose value is & < > " ' or : (319; sha256 of the list joined by newlines 19d03e077020c95bd42333c25946ed79aaf8fe3526f8c8408d3224c9d37f2916, which M5 recomputes). In that table no name, written with or without its ';', spells a SPECULATIVE_TERM or a SERVED_TERM, and over twelve contexts (a name inside spec_ulative, speculat_ive, what_if, scenario_view, hypo_thetical, counter_factual and serve_d, inside and after the --scenario flag, before and after speculative, and inside a served sentence) no name outside the list makes a hit decoded that it does not make written. At base b92d7a1 the census read 25 passed (25), and the gate's G09, G12, G13 and G14 mutants each read 25 passed (25). READ_FORMS (M6; wb-eu94, seat ws-03, run g10-work-s141, 2026-10-29): every row's page reading was measured by rendering its text with marked 18.0.11 (the repository's own dependency, default options) and parsing the HTML with parse5 7.1.2 (the HTML Standard's tokenizer and tree builder): the text nodes outside script, style, template, noscript and hidden or display:none elements, invisible code points dropped and NFKC applied, judged by the census's SPECULATIVE_TERM and SERVED_TERM. Its 40 joined rows read c1 and c2 true on the page and its 18 split and 10 over-read rows read false (marked shows each over-read row's form as written); the same reading gives every text of the Q10-Q13 quiet rows c1 and c2 true on the page except Q10's middle row, which marked escapes. Python's html.parser reads a CDATA section through ']]>', unlike the HTML Standard's bogus comment state, so the split CDATA row rests on parse5. Cut #2 (wb-eu94, seat ws-02, run g10-work-s145, 2026-10-30; refusal #1 at g10-gate-s144): the 117 appended READ_FORMS rows and the nine Q14 texts were read through the same oracle (marked 18.0.11 from the repository; parse5 7.1.2 and entities 4.5.0 installed outside the repository; the visible text nodes outside script, style, template, noscript and hidden elements, a space at each block element and a line break at br, invisible code points dropped, NFKC applied, judged by SPECULATIVE_TERM and SERVED_TERM): its 81 joined rows read c1 and c2 true on the page and its 18 split and 18 over-read rows false, and every Q14 text reads c1 and c2 true on the page while the view reads it false (the R-EDGE-GLUE escapes). The same oracle reproduces the 68 cut #1 labels and the refusal's measurements: its 330-case sweep case for case (42 under-read on the cut #1 view, none on this cut's), G01-G17 (under-read on cut #1, agreed on this cut) and its eight mutant witnesses. Cut #3 (wb-eu94, seat ws-01, run g10-work-s153, 2026-10-30; refusal #2 at g10-gate-s149, ruling R-B131): the 70 appended READ_FORMS rows and the added quiet-row texts (Q11's last two, Q13's last four, Q14's last seven, Q15-Q17) were read through the refusal #2 gate's page oracle, v2 (marked 18.0.11 from the repository renders; parse5 7.1.2 and entities 4.5.0, installed outside the repository, parse; the text nodes outside UA-hidden elements, a blank line at each edge of a block element and a line break at br, invisible code points dropped, NFKC applied, split by SENTENCE_BREAK and judged per unit by SPECULATIVE_TERM and SERVED_TERM): each appended row's c1 and c2 equal its page label (31 joined, 39 split); every quiet-row text the view reads false reads c2 true on the page, and c1 true too except Q14's x

M7's decoded values were read off parse5 7.1.2 by decoding each DECODE_PROBES code as '&#x;' inside a p element; Python 3.12.15 html._invalid_charrefs gives the same 0x80-0x9F values, and html.unescape the same value at 0, at the surrogates and past 0x10FFFF (it drops 0x7F, 0xFFFF and 0x10FFFF, which the HTML Standard keeps, so parse5 is the anchor). The table's 27 entries are the codes of 0x80-0x9F that parse5 replaces, written code=value in lowercase hex in code order and joined by line feeds; the digest is that text's sha256. Cut #4 (wb-eu94, seat ws-04, run g10-work-s160, 2026-10-31; refusal #3 at g10-gate-s156, ruling R-B175, the FAIL-CLOSED CORE): the 19 appended READ_FORMS rows, the 22 added M1 spellings, the 15 added M2 served-term inflections, the 11 added Q3 texts and Q14's added text were read through the refusal #3 gate's page oracle (gate-prep-23's tools/oracle.mjs and viewlib.mjs from its archive: marked 18.0.11 from the repository renders; parse5 7.1.2 and entities 4.5.0, installed outside the repository, parse; the text nodes outside UA-hidden elements, a blank line at each edge of a block element and a line break at br, invisible code points dropped, NFKC applied, split by SENTENCE_BREAK and judged per unit by SPECULATIVE_TERM and SERVED_TERM): each appended row's c1 and c2 equal its page label (11 joined rows read true on the page and in the view, 2 split rows false in both, 6 over-read rows false on the page and true in the view); each added M1 spelling reads c2 true on the page and in the view; each added M2 inflection reads SERVED_TERM true; each added Q3 text reads c1 false and c2 true on the page and in the view (the dot-numbered list item in 3 raw units, the sentence end splitting after its number too); Q14's added text reads c1 and c2 true on the page while the view reads c1 false and c2 true (the R-EDGE-GLUE escape at a line start). docsSpeculativeSentences: **RF speculation boundary:** rf's local default speculation policy stays passive/disabled and Pi documents no other default.

rf 0.1.845 ships `ResourceBrokerLimits` and `SpeculationBoundary` as values its host resource broker reads, with no CLI surface, and the one way an rf process opts into its speculative policy is the process-scoped `RF_ADAPTIVE` seat, which no rf child Pi launches receives: that child's environment holds only the `RF_CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST` names of `src/workbench/process-env.ts`.

Any Pi-declared SpeculationBoundary or broker-limit configuration may only tighten ResourceBrokerLimits and never overrides Pi host hard caps, the 60 s render deadline and the 256 KiB stdout and stderr bounds of `src/workbench/providers/reactivefiber.ts`.
